units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
She tries again to unclasp the bracelet , but fails .
Oh! don’t use big words. They mean so little.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Again tears at the bracelet in a paroxysm of rage , with inarticulate sounds .
Then stops , and looks at LORD GORING.
What are you going to do?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: I am going to ring for my servant. He is an admirable servant. Always comes in the moment one rings for him. When he comes I will tell him to fetch the police.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Trembling .
The police? What for?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: To-morrow the Berkshires will prosecute you. That is what the police are for.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Is now in an agony of physical terror .
Her face is distorted .
Her mouth awry .
A mask has fallen from her .
She is , for the moment , dreadful to look at .
Don’t do that. I will do anything you want. Anything in the world you want.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Give me Robert Chiltern’s letter.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Stop! Stop! Let me have time to think.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Give me Robert Chiltern’s letter.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I have not got it with me. I will give it to you to-morrow.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: You know you are lying. Give it to me at once.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: MRS. CHEVELEY pulls the letter out , and hands it to him .
She is horribly pale .
This is it?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: In a hoarse voice .
Yes.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Takes the letter , examines it , sighs , and burns it with the lamp .
For so well-dressed a woman, Mrs. Cheveley, you have moments of admirable common sense. I congratulate you.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Catches sight of LADY CHILTERN’S letter , the cover of which is just showing from under the blotting-book .
Please get me a glass of water.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Certainly.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Goes to the corner of the room and pours out a glass of water .
While his back is turned MRS. CHEVELEY steals LADY CHILTERN’S letter .
When LORD GORING returns the glass she refuses it with a gesture .
Thank you. Will you help me on with my cloak?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: With pleasure.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Puts her cloak on .
Thanks. I am never going to try to harm Robert Chiltern again.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Fortunately you have not the chance, Mrs. Cheveley.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Well, if even I had the chance, I wouldn’t. On the contrary, I am going to render him a great service.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: I am charmed to hear it. It is a reformation.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Yes. I can’t bear so upright a gentleman, so honourable an English gentleman, being so shamefully deceived, and so—
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Well?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I find that somehow Gertrude Chiltern’s dying speech and confession has strayed into my pocket.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: What do you mean?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: With a bitter note of triumph in her voice .
I mean that I am going to send Robert Chiltern the love-letter his wife wrote to you to-night.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Love-letter?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Laughing .
‘I want you. I trust you. I am coming to you. Gertrude.’
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: LORD GORING rushes to the bureau and takes up the envelope , finds is empty , and turns round .
You wretched woman, must you always be thieving? Give me back that letter. I’ll take it from you by force. You shall not leave my room till I have got it.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: He rushes towards her , but MRS. CHEVELEY at once puts her hand on the electric bell that is on the table .
The bell sounds with shrill reverberations , and PHIPPS enters .
After a pause .
